summary: User experience design for AI features and AI-first products, from prompt input to feedback loops.
abstract: An AI UX design agency designs the user experience (UX) and user interface (UI) of products that run on large language models (LLMs) or machine learning. Our team at ui-ux.agency, part of tkxel, maps where AI output enters a workflow, designs input, review and correction patterns, and tests them with real users in 4 to 10 weeks.

sections.h2: What does an AI UX design agency do?
sections.answer: An AI UX design agency designs how people give instructions to an AI system, read its output, judge whether it is right and fix it when it is wrong. The work sits between the model team and the people who use the product every day.
sections.body: A classic interface shows the same result for the same click. An AI feature returns a different answer each time, takes seconds to respond and is sometimes wrong with full confidence. Those three facts change the design brief. Our designers plan loading and streaming states, show where an answer came from, and give users a fast way to edit, retry or reject it. When the AI feature is a conversation, the work continues in chatbot UI design.

sections.h2: Which AI UX design problems does our agency solve?
sections.answer: Our AI UX design agency works on 5 problems that block adoption of AI features:

items.title: Blank-prompt paralysis.
items.body: Users stare at an empty input. We design starter prompts, templates and examples taken from real tasks.

items.title: Unclear trust.
items.body: Users cannot tell a good answer from a bad one. We add citations, source previews and plain-language confidence cues.

items.title: Slow responses.
items.body: Generation takes 3 to 20 seconds. We design streaming text, progress states and partial results so waiting feels shorter.

items.title: No way to correct.
items.body: A wrong answer forces a restart. We design inline edit, regenerate and undo, and we keep the user's work safe.

items.title: Silent failure.
items.body: The model refuses or drifts off topic. We write error and refusal states that tell users what to try next.

sections.h2: How does our AI UX design agency run a project?
sections.answer: An AI UX design project runs in 4 steps over 4 to 10 weeks, and each step ends with something the engineering team can use.

items.title: AI workflow mapping (1–2 weeks)
items.body: We interview users and map every point where the model reads data, writes output or makes a suggestion.

items.title: Interaction patterns (1–3 weeks)
items.body: We design input, output, review and correction patterns, including empty, loading, error and refusal states.

items.title: Prototype with real output (1–3 weeks)
items.body: Prototypes use real or recorded model responses, so testers react to genuine mistakes, not perfect sample text.

items.title: Testing and handoff (1–2 weeks)
items.body: 5 to 8 users run real tasks; we fix what fails and hand over specs, components and a pattern guide.

sections.h2: Which AI products does our AI UX design agency design?
sections.answer: Our AI UX design agency designs 4 types of AI products: copilots inside existing software, AI-first SaaS tools, AI agents that act for the user, and internal AI tools for operations teams.

items.title: Copilots
items.body: An assistant panel inside an existing product that drafts, summarizes or explains. Often part of a SaaS product redesign.

items.title: AI-first SaaS tools
items.body: Products where the model is the core feature, such as writing, analysis or search tools.

items.title: AI agents
items.body: Systems that take actions for the user. We design approval steps, activity logs and an easy stop button.

items.title: Internal AI tools
items.body: Tools that help support, finance or operations staff work through documents and tickets faster.

sections.h2: How much does an AI UX design agency cost?
sections.answer: AI UX design with our agency costs $25,000 to $90,000 and takes 4 to 10 weeks. The price depends on the number of AI features, user groups and platforms in scope.
sections.body: A single copilot feature inside an existing web app sits near $25,000. An AI-first product with several workflows, an admin area and a mobile view sits near $90,000. Teams that need design every sprint after launch can hire UI UX designers on a monthly plan. The full price breakdown sits in our UI UX design cost guide.

sections.answer: These answers cover the questions product teams ask before they hire an AI UX design agency.

faqs.q: Do you need a finished model before AI UX design starts?
faqs.a: No. We start with recorded outputs or a prototype prompt, and we update the design when the production model is ready.

faqs.q: Can an AI UX design agency work with our data science team?
faqs.a: Yes. Our designers join model reviews, read evaluation results and turn failure cases into interface states the engineers build.

faqs.q: How do you test AI features with users?
faqs.a: We give 5 to 8 users real tasks in a prototype that shows real model answers, including wrong ones, and we measure how often they accept, edit or reject each answer.

faqs.q: Which tools does your AI UX design team use?
faqs.a: Figma for design and prototypes, Maze for remote tests, and the OpenAI or Anthropic playgrounds to record real model responses for prototypes.
